$comment: Which Form IR dataTypes (form-ir-v0.1.md §2.1) a collection client can
actually present to an enumerator.
This is NOT the same question as 'is it in the IR', and conflating the two
is what defect 7 was. A dataType can be in the spec, carry a conformance
vector, and be evaluated identically by both engines — and still arrive on
a phone as a question nobody can answer, because the collection screen has
no widget for it. select_multiple was exactly that: spec §2.1, vector
select-001, both engines, and a label with empty space under it.
So there are three sets an XLSForm author needs told apart, and only the
second one answers 'will my question work in the field':
1. in the IR spec        — the document is valid, both engines evaluate it
2. collectable (this file) — a client can present it
3. neither               — not in the IR at all (rank, range)
Language-neutral and committed, for the same reason the conformance vectors
are: two hand-maintained copies drift, and this repository has already paid
for that once (SUBMISSION_STATUSES, which needed a test of its own to catch
the copy going stale). One file; a test on each side that fails when its
implementation and this file disagree:
Kotlin  CollectableTypesTest (:clients:composeApp:jvmTest) — drives the
real composable, in BOTH directions. A type listed here with no
branch is an unimplemented type claiming to work, which is the
worse failure; a branch not listed here is a type quietly working
that the importer's report calls unavailable.
Python  test_collectable_types.py — every entry is a real §2.1 dataType,
parsed out of the spec rather than hand-copied.
VERSIONED, because this is a fact about an app version and not a permanent
one. When barcode ships it belongs in v0.2, and a phone still running the
older build cannot collect it — which is precisely the case the collection
screen's `else` branch exists to make visible rather than silent. Nothing
here yet reports a device's version to the server; the shape is left so
that it can (sync §4 registration is the obvious place).
$choiceSourcesComment: Form IR §3 gives a select two ways to get its options, and a client has to
implement each of them separately. `inline` is the items in the document;
`dataset` names a key resolved against reference data the device holds.
The same defect-7 shape as the type list, one axis over: `select_one` is a
collectable dataType, and a *dataset-backed* select_one is not collectable
at all today — CollectionViewModel reads `node.choices?.items`, which is
empty for a dataset-backed list, so the question renders with no options
and the enumerator has a label with empty space under it. Reporting it as
collectable because `select_one` is in the list above would be exactly the
conflation this file exists to prevent.
`dataset` joined this list when the collection screen began resolving
through the engine instead of reading `choices.items`. That one line is
what took eight questions in the UCL form from 'would arrive with nothing
under the label' to answerable, and the importer stopped reporting them
as unpresentable on the same day with no code change on either side —
which is what the file is for.
The list is still not the whole story for a dataset-backed select, and the
difference is size rather than kind: rendering 229 villages is ordinary
and rendering 37,852 is not, so the screen picks a searchable lazy list
above a threshold. That is a presentation decision and not a capability —
a client that got it wrong would be slow, not incorrect.

notes.note: Display only — it has no value (§2.1), so it is 'collectable' in the sense that a client can present it correctly, not in the sense that it stores an answer.
notes.boolean: In §2.1 and deliberately absent here: no widget yet. XLSForm has no boolean type of its own — yes/no questions arrive as select_one — so nothing imported needs it today.
notes.time: In §2.1, no widget yet. Appears in real ODK forms; first candidate for v0.2.
notes.audio: In §2.1 as a media reference. Capture is not built on any platform (docs/project-conventions.md).
notes.video: In §2.1 as a media reference. Capture is not built on any platform.
notes.file: In §2.1 as a media reference. No picker built.
notes.drawing: In §2.1 as a media reference. The signature canvas is the same widget and could serve it; not wired.
notes.dataset choices: Form IR §3. Resolved by both engines (item 4 part 3), delivered to a device (part 4), and rendered by the collection screen through `FormInstance.choices` — so a form using one imports, pins its data, and is collectable. Measured on a Pixel at 37,852 villages: see §3.2.
